extracted.intended_audience: European citizens and residents interested in petitioning the European Parliament / members of the public seeking information about the petitions process
extracted.subtask_short: submitting a petition to EU Parliament
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and portal landing information for members of the public (European citizens and residents) who want to submit or support a petition to the European Parliament and learn how petitions are treated by the Petitions Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the petitions process in the European Parliament is to ensure that you have the opportunity to communicate with Parliament and express your right to petition, which is one of the fundamental rights of all European citizens and residents, enshrined both in the Treaty and in the Charter of Fundamental Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement establishes that petitioning is a fundamental right for European citizens and residents; the page points to the Lisbon Treaty for further reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of petitions (reality check / measure institutional response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your petition allows Parliament, through its Petitions Committee, to conduct an ongoing reality check on the way in which European legislation is implemented and measure the extent to which the European institutions are responding to your concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies petitions are intended to raise concerns about implementation of EU legislation or institutional responses; petitions therefore should relate to matters where implementation or institutional action/inaction is at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: European citizens and residents
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to petition is described as 'one of the fundamental rights of all European citizens and residents'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The portal is addressed to European citizens and residents as the primary audience for submitting petitions; users should confirm their eligibility where required in the detailed submission guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core petition process components (submit / treatment / support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key process questions are highlighted: 'How do I submit a petition?', 'How is my petition treated?', and 'How do I support a petition?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site provides Quick Start Guides and procedural pages for each of these stages — submit, procedural handling by the Committee, and mechanisms for other people to support petitions. Users should consult those sections for step-by-step requirements and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related resources and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The portal points users to related materials: 'European Union alternatives to petitions', 'Search infringement decisions', 'Quick Start Guides', 'Committee on Petitions' website, and contact details for the Committee Secretariat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should be aware that petitions are one mechanism among others (e.g., infringement procedures) and that the portal provides links and contact points for additional information, context, and privacy policy details.
